title: A Multi-Model Framework for Synthesizing High-Fidelity Network Intrusion Data
summary: Combines several generators into one framework for producing network intrusion records that hold their statistical shape well enough to train detectors on. A customised CTGAN is the generation component the framework is built around.
evidence: the multi-model utilizes a custom CTGAN based on the original; this paper presents a CTGAN-based multi-model framework for synthesizing network intrusion data

title: DP-Tabula: Differentially Private Synthetic Tabular Data Generation with Large Language Models
summary: Generates differentially private tabular data by fine-tuning a language model rather than a GAN, training the foundation model under a privacy budget and sampling from it. CTGAN appears as prior art in the survey of GAN-based tabular generation the paper positions itself against.
evidence: the GAN framework is introduced among prior studies tailored to synthetic tabular data generation; DP-Tabula itself trains an LLM, not CTGAN

title: Evaluating Lightweight GAN- and Adapted CTGAN-Based Data Synthesis for Predictive Maintenance in High-Radiation Environments
summary: Predictive maintenance in high-radiation environments suffers from scarce sensor data, so this builds two generators and measures which produces training data that holds up. GAN-1 is CTGAN, adapted for the sensor setting, and Random Forest, kNN and XGBoost are trained on its output.
affiliations: Culham Science Centre; United Kingdom Atomic Energy Authority
evidence: we have used two different GANs to generate synthetic data; GAN-1 is CTGAN, as described in the original paper, adapted here for sensor data

title: GANs for Class-Imbalanced Data: A Meta-Analysis
summary: Reviews how generative adversarial networks have been applied to class imbalance across published studies, and what the reported gains actually rest on. Names the CTGAN repository as the source of both CTGAN and TVAE, the synthesizers the surveyed work relies on.
evidence: the CTGAN repository services the code for CT-GAN, the GAN-based synthesizer used to generate tabular data; the archive also services the code for CTGAN as well as TVAE

title: Augmentation and Evaluation of Geological Tabular Data Based on a Generative Adversarial Network
summary: Geoscience sampling is expensive, leaving datasets small and unbalanced, so this builds Geo-TabGAN to augment them and evaluates the result on the Bayan Obo deposit. The model is a tabular GAN in the CTGAN line, used to generate 709 rock-type records against an original set of 29 quartz samples.
affiliations: Chinese Academy of Sciences; Institute of Geology and Geophysics
Chinese Academy of Sciences; Institute of Geology and Geophysics
evidence: a total of 709 data points were generated using the Geo-TabGAN model; the model is based on a GAN for tabular data, rectifying the imbalance in the original 29-sample set

title: Generating Synthesized Attacks for Intrusion Detection Using Generative Models with Important Features
summary: Selects the features an XGBoost model finds important, then generates attack records over only those features so the synthetic traffic stays useful for detection. xg-CTGAN and xg-CopulaGAN are the two generators built this way and evaluated with three classifiers.
evidence: we evaluate the effectiveness of xg-CTGAN and xg-CopulaGAN using three classifiers; the generated data by xg-CTGAN and xg-CopulaGAN improves classifier performance
